name: Amazon S3 (document files)

inputs.name: region
inputs.label: AWS region of the bucket (e.g. eu-central-1)

inputs.name: mapping
inputs.label: EDML mapping
hint: EDML mapping: a .json file or a folder of them on this computer.
Leave empty and the kit drafts it from the bucket after you give the access key.

inputs.name: access_key_id
inputs.label: Access key ID (Enter if the credential file holds it)

access: S3: s3:ListBucket on the mapped prefixes and s3:GetObject on the objects
tips: Tables and columns are named by the mapping file: a change to the mapping needs a new connect (exakit source remove <name>, then connect again).
A CSV mapping without fields has its columns inferred, and a date then arrives as VARCHAR(2000000): name the fields and their types in the mapping to get typed columns.
notes: The credential is an access key: the secret key alone on standard input (with --set access_key_id=...), or a JSON file through --password-file - what `aws iam create-access-key` prints, or `aws sts` temporary credentials with their session token. The kit never reads ~/.aws.

The account needs s3:ListBucket on the mapped prefixes and s3:GetObject on the objects (plus kms:Decrypt for a KMS-encrypted bucket). Measured: a prefix outside the policy fails as AccessDenied naming the action.

Standard regional endpoints over verified HTTPS only: no endpoint override, path-style access or anonymous reads. A bucket name with dots is refused, because its virtual-hosted name does not match the S3 certificate.

The adapter detects the file type by extension (.json, .jsonl, .csv, .parquet); CSV and Parquet can infer their columns, JSON needs explicit fields. A source glob that matches no file reads as an empty table - the check names such tables.
